newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to expand domestic LNG supply - ministry.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to expand domestic LNG supply - ministry.

text.p: South Korea plans to expand liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply for home fuel to four southern cities by the end of this year, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said on Wednesday.
The plan would raise the nation's LNG supply level to 40 percent from 35.9 percent at present, a ministry official said.
The four cities are Kyongju, Pusan, Ulsan and Kumi. Seoul and surrounding areas are currently provided with LNG.

As South Korea is turning away from other home fuels such as liquefied petroleum gas and to natural gas nationwide, LNG demand is likely to grow sharply, the official said. Official figures show South Korea's LNG demand rising to an estimated 9.7 million tonnes this year, 15.4 million in 2000, 19.5 million in 2006 and 23.3 million in 2010, against 7.1 million in 1995.
